## Blogs

**[Stephen Macedo And Frances Lee: Defend Your Essay That Dr. Jay Bhattacharya Would Restore Trust in Public Health](https://sciencebasedmedicine.org/macedo-lee-maha-maga-fluffers/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=macedo-lee-maha-maga-fluffers)** — *Science-Based Medicine*  
- Critique of a 2024 essay praising Jay Bhattacharya as a trust-restoring scientific leader; argues Bhattacharya advocated herd immunity via mass infection, opposed vaccines/masks, and aligned with RFK Jr./MAHA movement.  
- Contends the essay overlooked Bhattacharya’s “copious disinformation” and that MAHA proponents have gained credibility despite failed COVID predictions.  
- Warns anti-vaccine sentiment is expanding beyond COVID to childhood immunizations, risking measles/polio resurgence.

## News

**[Opinion: I led the FDA’s food safety and nutrition center. Here’s what people are missing about the cyclospora outbreak](https://www.statnews.com/2026/07/24/cyclospora-outbreak-contradiction-eat-real-food-less-safety-monitoring/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*  
- Former FDA CFSAN director Susan Mayne argues consumers shouldn’t face a trade-off between nutrition and food safety; calls for stronger monitoring infrastructure amid cyclospora outbreaks linked to fresh produce.

**[FDA advisory panel narrowly rejects compounding of one peptide, backs two others](https://www.statnews.com/2026/07/24/fda-peptide-compounding-panel-backs-epitalon-rejects-emideltide/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*  
- FDA Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted against including emideltide on the 503A bulk list, but supported epitalon and a third peptide (not named in body).  
- RFK Jr. has publicly endorsed peptides and stated he takes them himself, adding political visibility to the compounding review.

## Papers & Preprints

**[Elevation of anticancer drug-induced cytotoxicity by velpatasvir through downregulation of claudin-14 expression in human colorectal cancer cells](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501891/)** — *PubMed*  
- HCV NS5A inhibitor velpatasvir potentiates cytotoxicity of anticancer agents (e.g., 5-FU, oxaliplatin) in CRC lines by suppressing claudin-14, a tight-junction protein.  
- Suggests a repurposing avenue: velpatasvir may overcome chemoresistance via claudin-14–mediated pathways.

**[A framework and shared vocabulary to identify actionable protein biomarkers and enable optimal precision medicine: Myth-Busting with Unicorn Biomarkers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501868/)** — *PubMed*  
- Proposes a standardized framework and vocabulary for evaluating protein biomarkers’ clinical actionability, addressing reproducibility and “unicorn” (overhyped) biomarker claims.  
- Aims to harmonize discovery, verification, and validation stages for precision-medicine adoption.

**[Phase II Multicenter Clinical Trial of Intraoperative Molecular Imaging with Abenacianine During Lung Cancer Surgery](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42502096/)** — *PubMed*  
- Multicenter phase II trial evaluates abenacianine (a fluorescent imaging agent) for real-time tumor margin detection during lung cancer resection.  
- Primary endpoints include sensitivity/specificity of fluorescence guidance and impact on margin status.

**[A baseline systemic inflammatory signature predicts anti-PD-1 response in advanced melanoma](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501206/)** — *PubMed*  
- Identifies a pre-treatment systemic inflammatory signature (specific analytes not detailed in abstract) that correlates with response to anti-PD-1 therapy in advanced melanoma.  
- Potential blood-based biomarker to stratify patients for checkpoint inhibition.

**[Prioritizing Chemotherapy in Total Neoadjuvant Therapy Improves pCR Rate in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer in Countries with Limited Radiotherapy Access: A Randomized Controlled Trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501213/)** — *PubMed*  
- RCT in radiotherapy-limited settings shows sequencing chemotherapy before chemoradiation in total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) yields higher pathologic complete response (pCR) rates vs. standard TNT.  
- Supports chemotherapy-first TNT as a feasible strategy where radiation capacity is constrained.

**[Redox-regulated cell death in gastric cancer: Molecular insights and therapeutic opportunities](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501207/)** — *PubMed*  
- Review outlines ferroptosis, cuproptosis, disulfidptosis, and other redox-dependent death modalities in gastric cancer; maps molecular regulators (GPX4, FSP1, etc.) and highlights small-molecule inducers in preclinical development.

**[Biointegrated Battery-Based Electroceuticals](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501293/)** — *PubMed*  
- Review on implantable, battery-powered electroceutical devices for closed-loop neuromodulation and drug delivery; covers materials, power management, and translational hurdles for chronic use.

**[Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501282/)** — *PubMed*  
- Phase 2/3 data (abstract only) on Omicron BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 booster: immunogenicity non-inferior vs. ancestral strain vaccine, with comparable reactogenicity in both primed and naive adults.

**[Marine-Derived Nanocarriers for Immunomodulatory Drug Delivery: a Review On Convergence of Marine Pharmacology and Nanotechnology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501280/)** — *PubMed*  
- Surveys marine-sourced nanomaterials (chitosan, alginate, marine lipids, exosomes) as carriers for immunomodulatory agents; discusses targeting, biocompatibility, and scale-up challenges.

**[Advancing Cerebro-cerebellar Network Imaging with Ultra-high Field (7T) MRI: Progress and Future Challenges](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501259/)** — *PubMed*  
- Review of 7T MRI advances for resolving cerebro-cerebellar circuits; highlights applications in ataxia, autism, and psychosis, plus technical barriers (SAR, susceptibility, standardization).

**[Early Warning and Behavioural Intervention on the Cardiovascular Disease Risk in People Living with HIV: A Multicentre Non-Randomized Controlled Trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42502148/)** — *PubMed*  
- Non-randomized trial tests a CVD risk-alert system plus lifestyle intervention in PLWH; reports improvements in risk-factor control (lipids, BP, smoking) vs. usual care at 12 months.

**[Using Historical Blood Eosinophil Counts to Guide Treatment Decisions in Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501940/)** — *PubMed*  
- Retrospective analysis supports using longitudinal eosinophil trajectories (not single values) to predict ICS response and exacerbation risk in COPD.

**[Slowing myopia progression with a novel spectacle lens - 1-year, randomized double-masked, cross-over clinical trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501949/)** — *PubMed*  
- 1-year crossover RCT shows a novel defocus-incorporated spectacle lens reduces axial elongation and spherical equivalent progression vs. single-vision lenses in children.

**[Dentato-Rubro-Thalamic Tract-Targeted Cerebellar Deep Brain Stimulation for Post-Stroke Spasticity and Dystonia: preliminary experience](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42501340/)** — *PubMed*  
- Small case series uses tractography-guided cerebellar DBS targeting the dentato-rubro-thalamic tract; reports reduced spasticity/dystonia scores with acceptable safety.

## X / Twitter

**[🧬 Biopharma 𝕏 Weekly Recap](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2081125123285762393)** — *@BioStocks*  
- Novo Nordisk sues Eli Lilly over allegedly misleading GLP-1 ads and dose-comparison mismatches.  
- Nektar initiates Phase 3 ZENITH AD trials for rezpegaldesleukin (IL-2 agonist).  
- Tempus (TEM) acquires Personalis (PSNL) for $1.5B, bringing NeXT MRD platform in-house.  
- FDA advisory committee reviewing seven peptides for compounding (impacts HIMS, LFMD).  
- Multiple catalysts: HELP MDD data Q4, MPLT schizophrenia data mid-August, IOVA ESMO readouts, PRME IND clearance for Wilson disease PM577a.

**[Biotech IPO gains crush AI listings with standout 55% return](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2081009071793291392)** — *@BioStocks*  
- Biotech IPOs YTD 2026 show ~55% average return vs. AI listings; >$5B raised.  
- Notable tickers: MANE, COAG, SCTX (PCSK9 gene-editing IPO raised $129M upsized).

---

**Worth watching:** FDA peptide-compounding decisions (affects telehealth formularies), Tempus/Personalis integration of MRD into oncology data layer, and rezpegaldesleukin Phase 3 readout for atopic dermatitis.

- Biology & Health
    - [Pancreatic Cancer Risk](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/DFwdYtGQ56Q) -- Physionic
        - Higher blood glucose levels, including within the high-normal range, are associated with increased incidence of pancreatic pre-cancerous cysts and pancreatic cancer, with risk rising stepwise across the glycemic spectrum from normoglycemia to pre-diabetes to type 2 diabetes.  
        - Both the magnitude (intensity) and duration of hyperglycemia independently contribute to risk, as shown in a 10-year cohort of nearly 4 million individuals.  
        - A 22-million-person study confirmed a dose-response relationship between fasting glucose and pancreatic cancer risk, supporting elevated blood sugar as an independent risk factor despite observational limitations.  
        - Maintaining fasting glucose below 90 mg/dL (5 mmol/L) through exercise, nutrition, weight maintenance, and increased lean muscle mass is proposed as a primary prevention target.  
        - An unexplained, significant rise in blood sugar may serve as an early warning signal for pancreatic cancer, warranting urgent clinical evaluation, particularly in individuals with pancreatitis history, genetic susceptibility, or family history.
    - [Insurance Companies & AI Scribes | HealthTech #DadJokes](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/CMG0kiN-mIo) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Episode 6 of the weekly "HealthTech Dad Jokes" series hosted by Alex Koshykov and Sergei Polevikov
        - Satirical segment targeting health insurance companies and the AI scribe market within the digital health startup ecosystem
        - Aimed at professionals in healthcare, digital health, healthcare AI, health IT, venture capital, and startups
        - Released as a recurring Friday short-form humor series on YouTube
- Pure Science
    - [Why does every mammal get 1 billion heartbeats in their life?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tL9Lw250spc) -- Veritasium
        - The video explores how metabolic rate scales with body mass across mammals, tracing the historical shift from the surface-area-to-volume "surface law" (mass^2/3) to Kleiber's Law, which shows metabolic rate scales as mass^3/4.  
        - It details the West-Brown-Enquist (WBE) model, which derives the 3/4 exponent from fractal-like, space-filling vascular networks that minimize energy loss while supplying cells, assuming invariant terminal units (capillaries) and area-preserving or area-increasing branching.  
        - The model predicts that lifespan scales as mass^1/4 and heart rate as mass^-1/4, so the product — total heartbeats per lifetime — is roughly constant at ~1 billion across mammals.  
        - Humans are a major outlier, living ~2-3× longer than predicted (≈2-3 billion heartbeats), attributed to extended post-reproductive survival, medical advances, and social structures that reduce extrinsic mortality.  
        - The video examines whether the 3/4 exponent is truly universal, presenting critiques (e.g., Dodds, Glazier) that empirical data often fit 2/3 or vary by taxonomic group, and extends scaling concepts to cities, where infrastructure scales sublinearly (exponent ~0.85) while innovation scales superlinearly (~1.15).
